repos.name: microsoft/ai-agents-for-beginners
repos.description: 18 Lessons to Get Started Building AI Agents
repos.one_liner: A comprehensive 18-lesson curriculum designed to teach the fundamentals of building AI agents.
bullets: Structured as a series of Jupyter Notebooks covering agentic workflows and orchestration.
Focuses on core concepts like planning, memory, and tool-use in AI systems.
Ideal for developers transitioning from simple LLM prompting to autonomous agent development.
Provides a standardized educational framework for enterprise-grade AI integration.

repos.name: t8y2/motty
repos.description: SSH, SFTP, port forwarding, VNC/RDP and an AI assistant、MCP in one native window — a Go desktop app built on Viva, with no webview.
repos.one_liner: A high-performance, native Go desktop application that consolidates SSH, SFTP, port forwarding, and AI assistance into one window.
bullets: Built with Go and the Viva UI framework, avoiding heavy webview overhead.
Integrates Model Context Protocol (MCP) to allow AI assistants to interact with local infrastructure.
Streamlines remote server management and network tunneling for DevOps and infrastructure engineers.
Provides a unified interface for managing complex remote connections and AI-driven troubleshooting.

repos.name: mankidev/antialgorithm
repos.description: Claude Code skill that steers the model away from its first, most average pick in creative work: names, copy, ideas, posters, UI.
repos.one_liner: A Claude Code skill designed to force LLMs to bypass 'average' outputs in creative and technical decision-making.
bullets: Python-based tool that injects steering logic into the Claude Code agentic workflow.
Specifically targets the 'first-pick' bias inherent in LLMs to improve output quality.
Useful for developers and quant researchers who need to generate non-obvious solutions or unique code patterns.
Demonstrates advanced prompt engineering and agentic control techniques.
repos.img_alt: Six posters without the skill on top, six with it below
repos.img2_alt: Chart of how often a choice gets picked: a tall peak around the average marked as the safe zone, flat on both sides

repos.name: interfere-inc/landmines
repos.description: Oxlint rules that keep AI-written code honest: real implementations, real signals, no flake masking.
repos.one_liner: A set of Oxlint rules designed to detect and prevent AI-generated code from introducing subtle bugs or 'flake' patterns.
bullets: Built on the high-performance Oxlint engine for rapid static analysis.
Enforces code integrity by flagging common AI hallucination patterns and non-idiomatic implementations.
Essential for teams integrating AI-assisted coding into production-grade infrastructure.
Ensures that AI-written code adheres to strict project standards and real-world reliability requirements.

repos.name: erkamyaman/rust-anything
repos.description: Rewrite your whole app in Rust, one piece at a time, checked against the original's recorded behavior at every step. CLIs, HTTP servers and libraries in TypeScript, Python, C, Go, Ruby and Java.
repos.one_liner: A systematic framework for migrating legacy codebases to Rust while ensuring functional parity through automated verification.
bullets: Uses a 'check-at-every-step' methodology to validate behavior against original implementations.
Supports migration of CLIs, HTTP servers, and libraries from Python, TypeScript, Go, and more.
Provides a low-risk path for refactoring critical financial or infrastructure components into memory-safe Rust.
Focuses on maintaining system reliability during complex architectural transitions.
